chapter_theme: One song at Maruthuvakkudi (மருத்துவக்குடி): a plea against deceitful courtesans and the poet's own deafness to good counsel, asking for the feet that give realization of the meaning of the ancient sayings; Murugan is praised as the jnana guru of Siva.

849.reading: The poet speaks of vain women who pursue the arts of lust, deceitful tricksters and sweet-talkers with cloud-dark hair, in whose sidelong glance he turned and was ruined, and calls himself a low man who will not hear wise counsel, full of craving and bonds, a fool who does not grasp the true thing; he asks for the feet so that he may gain the great realization that gives the good meaning of the lofty old sayings. The praise names the vel against Sura and the arrogant demons, Murugan who loves the triple-Tamil garland sung by the pure who reached Siva, the jnana guru in the mind of Siva the trident-bearer, at Maruthuvakkudi where jackfruit juice floods the fields.
849.nuance: உரைத்த புத்திகள் கேளா நீசன் ... உளத்தில் மெய்ப்பொருள் ஓரா மூடன்: the poet blames himself for not heeding counsel, and asks for the feet so that the sense of the மூதுரை, the old sayings, may become his own experience (உணர்ச்சி). அரர் மனத்து இயல்படு ஞான தேசிக: Murugan as the jnana teacher in Siva's mind.
